n7e030e627f9.s: Which of the following monetary aggregates is the most liquid?
n7e030e627f9.x: Liquidity declines in the order M1, M2, M3, M4, so M1 is the most liquid and M4 the least.

nindian-economy-41-3.s: An increase in the SLR reduces the investible loan funds of commercial banks because it:
o: locks a greater percentage of bank funds in liquid assets
raises the rate at which banks borrow overnight
cuts the interest banks pay on deposits
lowers the currency held by the public
nindian-economy-41-3.x: A higher SLR locks more of the banks' funds in liquid assets, leaving less to lend.

nindian-economy-38-8.s: When ₹1 lakh is withdrawn in cash from a demand deposit account, currency with the public rises by ₹1 lakh and demand deposits:
nindian-economy-38-8.x: Demand deposits fall by ₹1 lakh as currency with the public rises by ₹1 lakh, so total money supply stays the same.

naaa7eac8379.s: Post-office deposits, term money and CDs of financial institutions, and public deposits of NBFCs are added in which aggregates?
naaa7eac8379.x: The broader liquidity aggregates L1–L3 add post-office deposits, term money and CDs of FIs, and NBFC public deposits.

nd181de1d1c8.s:
Consider the following statements about the LAF corridor:
1. The SDF forms the floor of the corridor.
2. The repo rate lies above the MSF rate.
3. The MSF and the bank rate are aligned at the ceiling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nd181de1d1c8.x: The SDF is the floor, the repo rate lies above it, and the MSF and bank rate sit at the ceiling; statement 2 is wrong because the repo rate is below the MSF.

nindian-economy-38-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the bank rate?
o: A lower bank rate is associated with expansionary monetary conditions
A lower bank rate makes borrowing cheaper
A lower bank rate is a contractionary move
A lower bank rate expands liquidity
nindian-economy-38-3.x: A lower bank rate makes borrowing cheaper and adds liquidity, so it is expansionary, not contractionary.

n9a97f7e2410.s: Which approach to monetary policy prevailed in India during 1998–2014?
n9a97f7e2410.x: Monetary targeting (1985–1998) was followed by the multiple-indicator approach (1998–2014), the glide path (2014–2016) and FIT from 2016.

n1e8a930b9ac.s:
Consider the following statements about the flexible inflation-targeting framework:
1. The Central Government sets the inflation target.
2. The RBI conducts monetary policy to achieve the target.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n1e8a930b9ac.x: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement divides the work: the Government sets the target and the RBI conducts monetary policy to achieve it.

new.s: The Digital Rupee became legal tender under the RBI Act through an amendment made by the:
new.x: The RBI Act was amended by the Finance Act 2022 to make the Digital Rupee legal tender.

new.s: Notes and coins that have no intrinsic value and are money by government order are called:
new.x: Fiat money has no intrinsic value; it is money because the government orders it.

new.s: Which authority issues the ₹1 note in India?
new.x: The ₹1 note and coins are issued by the Government of India; the remaining notes are issued by the RBI.

new.s: Under the Minimum Reserve System for note issue, of the ₹200 crore of gold and forex, gold must be at least:
new.x: The Minimum Reserve System needs ₹200 crore of gold and forex, of which ₹115 crore must be gold.

new.s: In which year was note issue transferred to the Reserve Bank of India?
new.x: Note issue passed to the RBI in 1935; 1861 gave the Government the monopoly of note issue.

new.s: The 1978 demonetisation of high-denomination notes was carried out under which Prime Minister?
new.x: The High Denomination Bank Notes (Demonetisation) Act, 1978 came under Morarji Desai.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (year – notes demonetised) is correctly matched?
new.x: 1978 withdrew ₹1,000, ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 notes; 2016 withdrew ₹500 and ₹1,000, and 1946 withdrew ₹1,000 and ₹10,000.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2016 demonetisation:
1. Curbing counterfeit currency (FICN) was one of its stated objectives.
2. The Supreme Court upheld it by a 4:1 majority in 2023.
3. The ₹2,000 notes withdrawn in May 2023 ceased to be legal tender.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Black money, FICN, corruption and terror financing were its objectives and the SC upheld it 4:1; the ₹2,000 notes withdrawn in May 2023 are still legal tender.

new.s: According to NCRB Crime in India 2024, the value of fake Indian currency notes (FICN) seized was about:
new.x: NCRB Crime in India 2024 records about ₹54.61 crore of fake currency seized.

new.s: Which of the following is a component on the sources side of reserve money?
o: Net foreign exchange assets of the RBI
new.x: Net forex assets of the RBI are on the sources side; the other three are on the uses side.

new.s: 'Other deposits with the RBI', a part of high-powered money, include deposits of:
new.x: Other deposits include those of quasi-government bodies, FIs, foreign central banks and governments, and international agencies such as the IMF; banks' deposits are bankers' deposits.

new.s: The new monetary aggregates NM0–NM3 (1998) are:
o: residency-based, separating short-term from long-term deposits
based on gold backing of currency
limited to currency with the public
new.x: NM0–NM3 are residency-based and separate short-term from long-term deposits.

new.s: M4 is M3 plus all post-office deposits, excluding:
new.x: M4 = M3 + all post-office deposits excluding NSCs.

new.s: When the public deposits currency in banks, money supply:
new.x: Depositing currency only moves money from currency to deposits, so money supply does not rise.

new.s: The quantity theory equation MV = PT is associated with:
new.x: MV = PT is Fisher's quantity theory; M = kPY is the Cambridge cash-balance equation of Marshall and Pigou.

new.s: The inventory (square-root rule) model of transactions demand for money is associated with:
new.x: The inventory model was given by Baumol (1952) and Tobin (1956).

new.s: The speculative demand for money varies with the rate of interest:
new.x: Speculative demand varies inversely with interest; at higher interest rates money demand falls.

new.s: The wholesale pilot of the e-Rupee (CBDC) began in:
new.x: The wholesale pilot began in November 2022 and the retail pilot in December 2022.

new.s: The money multiplier in India as on 31 December 2025 was:
new.x: On 31 Dec 2025 the money multiplier stood at 6.21.

new.s: The number of notes in circulation in May 2026 was about:
new.x: In May 2026, 174 billion notes worth over ₹42.12 lakh crore were in circulation.

new.s: Which of the following belongs to fiscal policy rather than monetary policy?
new.x: Repo, CRR and SLR are monetary instruments; fiscal deficit and public revenue belong to fiscal policy.

new.s: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) was introduced in:
new.x: LAF came in 2000; MSS in 2004, MSF in 2011 and SDF in 2022.

new.s: The multiple indicator approach to monetary policy was dropped mainly because it was:
new.x: It was opaque: markets could not predict the RBI when indicators conflicted.

new.s: Open Market Operations are the RBI's main tool for managing:
new.x: OMOs are the main tool for durable liquidity.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about credit control instruments:
1. Qualitative instruments regulate the direction of credit.
2. Quantitative instruments are also called selective credit control.
3. Bank rate is a quantitative instrument.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Qualitative tools regulate direction of credit and are the selective controls; bank rate is quantitative, so statement 2 is wrong.

new.s: When the MSF began in May 2011, its rate was set at the repo rate plus:
new.x: MSF began in May 2011 at repo + 100 bps; it is now repo + 25 bps.

new.s: The MSF rate was aligned with the Bank Rate in:
new.x: The MSF was aligned to the Bank Rate in February 2012.

new.s: Among NBFCs, which entities can access the RBI's LAF?
new.x: Only Primary Dealers, classed as NBFCs, have access to the LAF.

new.s: A 'hawkish' monetary-policy stance indicates that the central bank:
o: is worried about inflation and tightens
is worried about growth and eases
has stopped using the repo rate
new.x: Hawkish = worried about inflation, tightening; dovish = worried about growth, easing bias.

new.s: The 25 per cent statutory floor on SLR was removed by the:
new.x: The BR (Amendment) Act, 2007 removed the 25% SLR floor; SLR now ranges 0–40% of NDTL.

new.s: The penalty on a bank for an SLR shortfall is initially:
new.x: An SLR shortfall attracts bank rate + 3%, rising to bank rate + 5% if it continues.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the SLR:
1. MSS securities count towards the SLR.
2. The SLR is governed by Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: MSS securities count towards SLR; SLR is under Section 24 of the BR Act 1949, while Section 42 of the RBI Act governs CRR.

new.s: To control inflation through open market operations, the RBI will:
new.x: Selling G-secs is the dear-money OMO; buying G-secs is expansionary.

new.s: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) began operating in:
new.x: The SDF was proposed in 2015, enabled by Budget 2018-19 and began in April 2022.

new.s: The temporary 10 per cent incremental CRR of August 2023 impounded about:
new.x: The I-CRR of 10 Aug 2023 impounded about ₹1.1 lakh crore.

new.s: How many fine-tuning operations did the RBI conduct in FY24?
new.x: The RBI ran 49 fine-tuning operations in FY24.

new.s: On 4 September 2026, the RBI absorbed ₹6.02 lakh crore of surplus liquidity through:
new.x: With surplus near ₹10.32 lakh crore, the RBI absorbed ₹6.02 lakh crore via two 3-day VRRRs.

new.s: The Prime Lending Rate (PLR), introduced in 1994, was set by:
new.x: The PLR was the rate for best borrowers set by each bank; the RBI does not fix the PLR.

new.s: The Janak Raj Internal Study Group (2017) found weak MCLR transmission and recommended:
o: an external benchmark for lending rates
a return to the Base Rate
new.x: It found MCLR transmission weak and recommended an external benchmark, leading to the EBLR mandate.

new.s: Through the exchange-rate channel, a repo-rate cut works mainly by:
new.x: Under the exchange-rate channel a rate cut weakens the rupee, which helps exports.

new.s: After the 125 bps repo cut (Feb 2025–Feb 2026), the weighted average lending rate on fresh loans fell by about:
new.x: Fresh-loan WALR fell about 93 bps: about 80 bps from rate changes and 13 bps from loan mix.

new.s: Which obstacle to monetary transmission holds bank deposit rates up?
new.x: Administered small-savings rates hold deposit rates up and slow transmission.

new.s: Compared with monetary policy, fiscal policy acts slowly mainly because of:
new.x: Fiscal policy suffers legislative and implementation lags; monetary policy acts quickly (bi-monthly).

new.s: Supply-driven food inflation is best tackled through:
o: fiscal steps such as buffer-stock releases and duty cuts
new.x: Monetary tools act on demand; supply-driven food inflation needs fiscal steps like buffer stocks and duty cuts.

new.s: Which of the following is true of fiscal policy compared with monetary policy?
o: It is made by the RBI
Its effect is direct but slow
new.x: Fiscal policy is made by the Government, acts directly but slowly due to legislative lags; monetary policy is by the RBI/MPC, indirect and quick.

new.s: The S. S. Tarapore Committee of 1997 dealt with:
new.x: Tarapore (1997; second in 2006) dealt with capital account convertibility.

new.s: In which year did the Urjit Patel Committee recommend flexible inflation targeting?
new.x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended FIT with 4% ±2% CPI.

new.s: The Urjit Patel Committee recommended which index as the nominal anchor of monetary policy?
new.x: It recommended CPI-C as the nominal anchor; the anchor is CPI-C, not WPI.

new.s: The multiple-indicator approach (1998–2014) was criticised for being:
new.x: The multiple-indicator approach was criticised as opaque.

new.s: The 'Seven Ages of India's Monetary Policy' speech by Shaktikanta Das was delivered in:
new.x: Shaktikanta Das delivered the speech on 24 January 2020.

new.s: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI was signed on:
new.x: The MPFA was signed on 20 Feb 2015; the RBI (Amendment) Act came in May 2016.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement?
o: It was signed by the Government and the RBI
It formally adopted flexible inflation targeting
It is a statute enacted by Parliament
The RBI is answerable for missing the target
new.x: The MPFA (2015) is an agreement, not a statute; the statute is the RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016.

new.s: The 4 per cent inflation target was first notified in:
new.x: The target was first notified in August 2016 for the period to 31 March 2021.

new.s: The CPI-Combined, the anchor of the inflation target, is compiled by the:
new.x: Headline CPI-C is compiled by the NSO under MoSPI.

new.s: What is the quorum for a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee?
new.x: Quorum is 4, including the Governor or, in his absence, the Deputy Governor.

new.s: In case of a tie in the Monetary Policy Committee, the RBI Governor has:
new.x: The Governor chairs the MPC and has a casting vote on a tie, not a veto.

new.s: The one RBI officer on the Monetary Policy Committee is nominated by the:
new.x: The RBI officer is nominated by the RBI Central Board; external members are appointed by the Central Government.

new.s: The policy stance 'withdrawal of accommodation' signals:
o: a tightening bias that drains excess liquidity
new.x: Withdrawal of accommodation is a tightening bias that drains excess liquidity.

new.s: In December 2025, the policy repo rate was cut by 25 bps to:
new.x: In Dec 2025 the repo was cut 25 bps to 5.25% and held there through Aug 2026.

new.s: In June 2026, as major central banks geared up to tighten, the MPC:
o: held the repo at 5.25% and cut the FY27 growth forecast
new.x: In June 2026 the MPC held 5.25% and cut the FY27 growth forecast.
